# Every loop shape, written inside a test function rather than in the code
# under test, and run on a Go-backed target.
#
# A test body is lowered by its own emitter (codegen/lang/golang/testlower.go)
# so that test intrinsics inside a loop still get their own lowering. That
# emitter used to write the loop head itself, and it knew only the two shapes
# that existed when it was written: a counted loop came out as a range over a
# pull sequence with two variables (which Go refuses), a condition loop put the
# condition where the range operand goes, and `for { }` dereferenced an
# iterable that is not there and took the launcher down with it. The head is
# ForHead's now -- there is one right answer per IterKind, already written
# down once -- and this pins all five shapes through that path.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import "sngl:seq"

component main {
    text(value="hi")
}

func testForever(t Test) {
    var i = 0
    for {
        i = i + 1
        if i > 3 {
            break
        }
    }
    t.assert(i == 4)
}

func testCondition(t Test) {
    var j = 0
    for j < 4 {
        j = j + 1
    }
    t.assert(j == 4)
}

func testCounted(t Test) {
    var n = 0
    for var i = seq.count(4) {
        n = n + i
    }
    t.assert(n == 6)
}

func testIndexed(t Test) {
    var n = 0
    for var i, x = [5, 6] {
        n = n + i * x
    }
    t.assert(n == 6)
}

func testMapEntries(t Test) {
    var m map<string, int> = {"a" = 1, "b" = 5}
    var n = 0
    for var k, v = m {
        n = n + v + k.length() - 1
    }
    t.assert(n == 6)
}
